weekSubtitle: The Elements of Drama (Plays, Story vs. Drama, 8 Elements & Scenes)

lessons.title: Lesson 1: What is Drama? (Story vs. Play)
lessons.description: Learn what a drama and theater are, and compare a story book to a play: playwright, actors, and acts & scenes!
lessons.hint: A drama is a story acted out on stage for an audience!

cards.frontHint: Stories made to be acted out on stage!
cards.explanation: A drama is a play! Instead of only reading it silently in a book, actors perform a drama for an audience on a stage.
cards.example: Our class watched a drama about a brave knight on stage.
cards.tip: Think of the happy and sad theater masks 🎭 — drama means acting out a story!

cards.explanation: The drama (a play) is a story which can be performed for an audience on a stage or theater.
cards.example: A drama is a story performed for an audience on a stage.
cards.tip: An audience is the group of people sitting and watching the play!

cards.explanation: A theater is the stage where the play is performed.
cards.example: The theater has big red curtains around the stage.
cards.tip: When the red curtains open at the theater, you see the stage!

cards.explanation: In a story, the person who writes it is an author or writer. In a drama, the writer is called a playwright!
cards.example: A playwright wrote the castle play instead of a book author.
cards.tip: A 'wright' is someone who makes or builds something — a playwright builds a play!

cards.explanation: In a story, we read about characters. In a drama, actors dress up and perform as the characters on stage!
cards.example: The actors wore crowns to play the castle characters.
cards.tip: Characters in a story → Actors in a drama!

cards.explanation: In a story book, the story is split into chapters. In a drama, the play is split into acts and scenes!
cards.example: Instead of chapters, our play has two acts and four scenes.
cards.tip: Chapters in a story → Acts & scenes in a drama!

activity.title: Story vs. Drama Match!
activity.instruction: Tap a Story or Clue card on the left, then tap its matching Drama word on the right!
allPairs: Author or writer in a story

lessons.title: Lesson 2: The 8 Elements of Drama
lessons.description: Master all 8 parts from the Elements of Drama chart: Script, Cast, Narrator, Setting, Act, Scene, Dialogue, and Stage Directions!
lessons.hint: Look closely at what each part does: tells words, tells time/place, or tells actors what to do!

cards.frontHint: Every play is built from 8 special pieces!
cards.explanation: The 8 elements of drama are: Script, Cast of Characters, Narrator, Setting, Act, Scene, Dialogue, and Stage Directions.
cards.example: Every drama uses a script, setting, dialogue, and actors.
cards.tip: Tap Next to meet all 8 elements one by one!

cards.explanation: Script: the text (all the written words) of the play.
cards.example: Each actor holds a script to read the words of the play.
cards.tip: Without the script, nobody would know what to say or do!

cards.explanation: Cast of Characters: all of the characters in the play, usually portrayed (acted out) by actors.
cards.example: The cast of characters lists all the roles played by actors.
cards.tip: Check the top of a script to see the full Cast of Characters!

cards.explanation: Narrator: the person who tells what happens during the play.
cards.example: The narrator tells the audience what happens in the castle.
cards.tip: Think of the narrator as the friendly storyteller helping the audience!

cards.explanation: Setting: the time and place in the play.
cards.example: The setting of our play is a sunny treehouse in the afternoon.
cards.tip: Ask two questions for Setting: WHERE is it? WHEN is it?

cards.explanation: Act: a chapter in a play that contains more than one scene.
cards.example: Act 1 is a big part of the play that holds three short scenes.
cards.tip: Remember: an Act is BIGGER than a scene (one Act can hold 2, 3, or more scenes)!

cards.explanation: Scene: the action that takes place in a single setting.
cards.example: This scene takes place inside one cozy treehouse.
cards.tip: One scene stays in one single setting (one place and time)!

cards.explanation: Dialogue: the words said by the characters.
cards.example: Actors speak the dialogue out loud to tell the story.
cards.tip: Dialogue = talking! Notice 'di-' and think of characters talking together.

cards.explanation: Stage Directions: written instructions telling the actors what to do (like where to walk, or how to smile or whisper).
cards.example: Stage directions tell an actor to wave and walk to the door.
cards.tip: Stage directions tell actors WHAT TO DO — actors act them out instead of reading them aloud!

activity.title: Match all 8 Elements!
activity.instruction: Match each Element of Drama on the left with its meaning on the right!
allPairs: All of the characters, portrayed by actors
Person who tells what happens during the play
The time and place in the play
A chapter in a play with more than one scene
Action that takes place in a single setting
The words said by the characters
Written instructions telling actors what to do

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Scenes & Reading a Mini Script
lessons.description: Discover when a new scene starts (when time or place changes!) and spot clues inside a real mini script!
lessons.hint: Watch the setting! Does the time or place change?

cards.frontHint: One piece of the play in one place & time
cards.backTitle: A Scene is a Unit of the Play
cards.explanation: The scene is a unit (part) of the play that happens at a specific place or time.
cards.example: Scene 1 happens at a specific place and time in the treehouse.
cards.tip: Think of each scene like a snapshot at one place and one time!

cards.frontTitle: When is it a New Scene?
cards.frontHint: Watch for a change in TIME or PLACE!
cards.explanation: You will know it's a new scene when the time or place changes!
cards.example: You know a new scene starts when the time or place changes.
cards.tip: If EITHER the time OR the place changes, get ready for a new scene!

cards.frontHint: Castle in Scene 1 → Forest in Scene 2
cards.explanation: If the actors are inside a castle in Scene 1, and then the story moves out to a forest in Scene 2, the place changed — so it's a new scene!
cards.example: Moving from the castle to the forest starts a new scene.
cards.tip: Stage helpers often swap the backdrop when the place changes!

cards.frontHint: Morning in Scene 1 → Night in Scene 2
cards.explanation: Even in the same treehouse, if Scene 1 is sunny morning and Scene 2 jumps to starry night (or the next day), the time changed — so it's a new scene!
cards.example: Jumping from morning to night in the treehouse starts a new scene.
cards.tip: Check the sky or clock! Morning to night means a new scene!

cards.frontHint: Names show Dialogue • (Parentheses) show Stage Directions
cards.explanation: In a script, 'Maya: Hello!' is dialogue (spoken out loud). Words in parentheses like (waves happily) are stage directions telling the actor what to do!
cards.example: Stage directions tell Maya to wave before speaking her dialogue.
cards.tip: Do NOT read stage directions in (parentheses) out loud — act them out!

activity.title: New Scene & Script Detective!
activity.instruction: Read the play clue carefully, then tap the best answer!

items.prompt: In Scene 1, the kids are in a castle. Next, they are in a treehouse. What starts now?
items.explanation: Right! You know it's a new scene when the place or time changes.

items.prompt: Scene 1 happens in the treehouse at noon. Scene 2 happens in the treehouse at midnight. Why is it a new scene?
items.explanation: Yes! Even at the same place, a new scene starts when the time changes (noon → midnight).

items.prompt: Look at this line from a script: Which part is the DIALOGUE?
items.explanation: Dialogue is the words said out loud by the characters!

items.prompt: Look at this script line. What is '(jumps up and claps)'?
items.explanation: Stage directions are written instructions telling the actors what to do!

items.prompt: Who tells the audience what happens during the play?
items.explanation: The narrator is the person who tells what happens during the play!

items.prompt: Which part of a play is like a chapter that contains more than one scene?
items.explanation: An act is a chapter in a play that contains more than one scene!

practices.description: Practice matching Script, Cast of Characters, Narrator, Setting, Act, Scene, Dialogue, and Stage Directions!
practices.hint: Remember each clue: text = script, talking = dialogue, what to do = stage directions, time & place = setting.

practices.title: Practice 3: Scenes & Mini Script Detective
practices.description: Practice spotting scene changes (time or place!) and reading short mini play scripts!
practices.hint: A new scene begins whenever the time or place changes! Words in (parentheses) tell actors what to do.

quiz.title: Week 1 Final Quiz: Elements of Drama
quiz.description: A fun 10-question mix covering Drama, Theater, Story vs. Play, all 8 Elements, and Scene Changes!
quiz.hint: Read carefully, tap 🔊 if you want to listen, and think about how plays work on stage!
quiz.instruction: Read the question and tap the best answer!

questions.instruction: Choose the best definition of drama.
questions.text: What is a drama (a play)?
options: A story performed for an audience on a stage or theater
A list of math problems to solve silently
A dictionary full of spelling words
A song played only on the radio
questions.answer: A story performed for an audience on a stage or theater
questions.hint: Think about actors acting out a story in front of people watching!
questions.explanation: A drama (a play) is a story which can be performed for an audience on a stage or theater.

questions.instruction: Remember what we call the place where actors perform.
questions.text: What is a theater?
options: The stage where the play is performed
The front cover of a storybook
A paintbrush used in art class
The last sentence in a paragraph
questions.answer: The stage where the play is performed
questions.hint: Where do the red curtains open so actors can perform a play?
questions.explanation: A theater is the stage where the play is performed.

questions.instruction: Compare a story book to a drama.
questions.text: In a story, the writer is an author. Who writes a drama (a play)?
questions.hint: This special word starts with 'play' and means someone who builds a play!
questions.explanation: An author writes a story, and a playwright writes a drama (a play)!

questions.instruction: Compare a story book to a drama.
questions.text: In a story, we read about characters. Who plays the characters in a drama?
questions.hint: Real people put on costumes and perform on stage!
questions.explanation: Characters in a story are portrayed by actors in a drama!

questions.instruction: Compare a story book to a drama.
questions.text: A story book is divided into chapters. A drama is divided into ___.
questions.hint: Think of the big parts and smaller setting units in a play!
questions.explanation: Chapters in a story are like acts and scenes in a drama!

questions.instruction: Think about who watches the play.
questions.text: A drama is a story performed on a stage for an ___.
questions.hint: Who sits in the seats, watches the play, and claps at the end?
questions.explanation: Actors perform a drama for an audience on a stage or theater!

questions.instruction: Match Story vs. Drama.
questions.text: Which pair is a match for Story → Drama?
questions.hint: Who writes a story, and who writes a play?
questions.explanation: Author or writer in a story matches playwright in a drama!

questions.instruction: Match Story vs. Drama.
questions.text: Which pair correctly matches Chapters in a story?
options: Chapters in a story → acts and scenes
questions.answer: Chapters in a story → acts and scenes
questions.hint: Both divide the story into parts from beginning to end!
questions.explanation: Chapters in a story compare to acts and scenes in a drama!

questions.instruction: Think about what actors do on stage.
questions.text: A class puts on costumes and acts out 'The Castle Dragon' in front of parents. What are they performing?
questions.hint: A story acted out for an audience on stage is called a...
questions.explanation: A story performed in front of an audience on a stage is a drama (a play)!

questions.instruction: Use the word 'playwright' correctly.
questions.text: Nadia loves writing plays with dialogue and stage directions for her school stage. Nadia is a ___.
questions.hint: What do we call the writer of a drama?
questions.explanation: Someone who writes a play is called a playwright!

questions.instruction: Remember what a theater is.
questions.text: Sam steps behind the red curtains onto the stage where the play will be performed. Sam is in the ___.
questions.hint: Our slides say: A ___ is the stage where the play is performed.
questions.explanation: A theater is the stage where the play is performed!

questions.instruction: Compare Story vs. Drama.
questions.text: How is a drama DIFFERENT from a regular story book?
options: A drama is written to be performed by actors on a stage for an audience
A drama has no characters and no setting
A drama can only be three words long
A drama never has any talking
questions.answer: A drama is written to be performed by actors on a stage for an audience
questions.hint: Think about what happens in a theater!
questions.explanation: A drama (a play) is a story written to be performed for an audience on a stage or theater!

questions.instruction: Spot the Drama word.
questions.text: In a play about Robin Hood and Snow White on stage, the real people dressed up as Robin Hood and Snow White are the ___.
questions.hint: Who plays the characters on stage in a drama?
questions.explanation: The characters in a drama are portrayed by actors on stage!

questions.instruction: Fill in the Story vs. Drama blank.
questions.text: Author is to Story as ___ is to Drama.
questions.hint: An author writes a story. Who writes a play?
questions.explanation: An author writes a story, and a playwright writes a drama!

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: What is the script of a play?
questions.hint: All the written words that make up the play!
questions.explanation: Script = the text of the play!

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: What is the Cast of Characters?
options: All of the characters, usually portrayed by actors
The time and place of the play
The instructions telling the actors when to sit down
The first chapter in a book
questions.answer: All of the characters, usually portrayed by actors
questions.hint: Look at the word 'characters' right inside 'Cast of Characters'!
questions.explanation: Cast of Characters = all of the characters, usually portrayed by actors.

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: Who is the narrator in a play?
options: The person who tells what happens during the play
The person who sews the costumes
The building where the play happens
questions.answer: The person who tells what happens during the play
questions.hint: This person narrates (tells) what is happening to help the audience!
questions.explanation: Narrator = the person who tells what happens during the play!

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: What is the setting of a play?
options: The time and place in the play
All the words spoken out loud
questions.answer: The time and place in the play
questions.hint: Setting answers WHERE and WHEN!
questions.explanation: Setting = the time and place in the play!

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: What is an act in a play?
options: A chapter in a play that contains more than one scene
One single word spoken by an actor
Written instructions telling actors to smile
The place where the audience sits
questions.answer: A chapter in a play that contains more than one scene
questions.hint: It is a BIG section of a play made up of several smaller scenes!
questions.explanation: Act = a chapter in a play that contains more than one scene.

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: What is a scene in a play?
options: The action that takes place in a single setting
The entire book of every play ever written
The person who tells what happens
questions.answer: The action that takes place in a single setting
questions.hint: One scene stays in one single setting (one place and time)!
questions.explanation: Scene = the action that takes place in a single setting!

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: What is dialogue?
options: The words said by the characters
The painted castle behind the stage
The written directions that are NOT read aloud
The list of scenes at the start
questions.answer: The words said by the characters
questions.hint: Characters speak this out loud when talking in a play!
questions.explanation: Dialogue = the words said by the characters!

questions.instruction: Identify the element of drama.
questions.text: What are stage directions?
options: Written instructions telling the actors what to do
The street address of the theater
A song sung by the audience
The cover art of the script
questions.answer: Written instructions telling the actors what to do
questions.hint: They direct the actors on stage — telling them what to do!
questions.explanation: Stage Directions = written instructions telling the actors what to do!

questions.instruction: Choose the matching Element of Drama.
questions.text: Which element gives written instructions telling the actors to 'tiptoe quietly across the bridge'?
questions.hint: It tells the actors WHAT TO DO on stage!
questions.explanation: Telling an actor to tiptoe quietly is a stage direction!

questions.instruction: Choose the matching Element of Drama.
questions.text: Which element of drama is shown here? 'King: Welcome to my castle! Queen: Thank you for the party!'
questions.hint: These are the words spoken out loud by the King and Queen!
questions.explanation: The words said by the characters are called dialogue!

questions.instruction: Choose the matching Element of Drama.
questions.text: 'Time: A rainy Tuesday afternoon. Place: Inside Grandma's kitchen.' Which element is this?
questions.hint: It tells BOTH the time and place of the play!
questions.explanation: The time and place in a play is the setting!

questions.instruction: Choose the matching Element of Drama.
questions.text: 'Characters: Mia (a detective), Leo (her little brother), Whiskers (a talking cat).' What is this list called?
questions.hint: It lists all of the characters in the play!
questions.explanation: All of the characters in a play make up the Cast of Characters!

questions.instruction: Choose the matching Element of Drama.
questions.text: The teacher hands out stapled pages containing all the character names, dialogue, and stage directions for the class play. She is handing out the ___.
questions.hint: What do we call the text (written pages) of the whole play?
questions.explanation: The script is the text of the play!

questions.instruction: Choose the matching Element of Drama.
questions.text: During the play, one voice explains to the audience: 'Long ago, two friends sailed across the ocean looking for a hidden island.' Who is speaking?
questions.hint: Who tells what happens during the play?
questions.explanation: The narrator is the person who tells what happens during the play!

questions.instruction: Compare Act and Scene.
questions.text: Which statement about an Act and a Scene is TRUE?
options: An act is like a chapter and contains more than one scene
A scene contains ten acts inside it
Acts are only for story books, never for plays
An act is smaller than one single word
questions.answer: An act is like a chapter and contains more than one scene
questions.hint: Think: Act = big chapter; Scene = smaller unit inside it!
questions.explanation: An act is a chapter in a play that contains more than one scene!

questions.instruction: Remember the role of Stage Directions.
questions.text: In a play, should an actor read the stage directions in (parentheses) out loud to the audience?
options: No — stage directions are instructions showing the actor what to do
Yes — actors shout them louder than their dialogue
Yes — only the narrator must read every direction
No — actors skip them and do nothing
questions.answer: No — stage directions are instructions showing the actor what to do
questions.hint: If a script says (waves hand), does the actor say the word 'waves hand' or actually wave?
questions.explanation: Actors perform the stage directions instead of reading them out loud!

questions.instruction: Remember how a scene works.
questions.text: A scene is a unit of the play that happens at a specific ___.
questions.hint: Slide 6 says: The scene happens at a specific ___ or ___.
questions.explanation: The scene is a unit of the play that happens at a specific place or time!

questions.instruction: Remember the New Scene rule!
questions.text: How will you know it is a new scene in a play?
options: When the time or place changes
When an actor wears a green hat
When a character asks a question
When the playwright writes two commas
questions.answer: When the time or place changes
questions.hint: Slide 7 says: You will know it's a new scene when the ___ or ___ changes!
questions.explanation: You know it's a new scene when the time or place changes!

questions.instruction: Spot what causes a new scene.
questions.text: Scene 1 happens inside a treehouse. Next, the characters climb down and run into the park. Why does a new scene start?
options: Because the narrator forgot a line
questions.hint: They moved from the treehouse to the park — did time or place change?
questions.explanation: Moving from the treehouse to the park changes the place, starting a new scene!

questions.instruction: Spot what causes a new scene.
questions.text: Scene 1 takes place in the classroom on Monday morning. Scene 2 happens in the same classroom on Friday afternoon. Why is it a new scene?
options: Because the place moved to a castle
Because the script ran out of paper
questions.hint: The classroom stayed the same, so what changed from Monday morning to Friday afternoon?
questions.explanation: Even in the same place, changing from Monday morning to Friday afternoon changes the time — starting a new scene!

Narrator: King Omar looked everywhere for his shiny crown.
King Omar (scratching his head): Did anyone see my crown?
Princess Dina (pointing near the window): Look! A bluebird took it to the tree!

questions.text: What is the SETTING of Act 1, Scene 1?
options: Inside a sunny castle throne room in the morning
questions.answer: Inside a sunny castle throne room in the morning
questions.hint: Read sentence (1) of the script for the place and time!
questions.explanation: Sentence (1) tells us the setting (time & place): inside a sunny castle throne room in the morning!

questions.instruction: Read the mini script and answer the question.

passage.title: The Lost Crown — Act 1, Scene 1
sentences: Setting: Inside a sunny castle throne room in the morning.
Narrator: King Omar looked everywhere for his shiny crown.
King Omar (scratching his head): Did anyone see my crown?
Princess Dina (pointing near the window): Look! A bluebird took it to the tree!

questions.text: In sentence (3), what is '(scratching his head)'?
questions.hint: Words in (parentheses) tell the actor playing King Omar what to do!
questions.explanation: (scratching his head) is stage directions telling the actor what to do!

questions.instruction: Read the mini script and answer the question.

passage.title: The Lost Crown — Act 1, Scene 1
sentences: Setting: Inside a sunny castle throne room in the morning.
Narrator: King Omar looked everywhere for his shiny crown.
King Omar (scratching his head): Did anyone see my crown?
Princess Dina (pointing near the window): Look! A bluebird took it to the tree!

questions.text: In sentence (2), who is telling the audience what happened?
questions.hint: Look at the label at the start of sentence (2)!
questions.explanation: The narrator tells what happens during the play!

questions.instruction: Read the mini script and answer the question.

passage.title: The Lost Crown — Scene 1 & Scene 2
sentences: Scene 1 Setting: Inside the castle throne room in the morning.
Princess Dina: Let's climb up to the tall treehouse outside!
Scene 2 Setting: Outside in the garden treehouse at noon.
King Omar (smiling): Hurray! My crown is safe in the bird nest!

questions.text: How do you know Scene 2 is a NEW scene?
options: Both the place (treehouse) and time (noon) changed
The script became a chapter book
questions.answer: Both the place (treehouse) and time (noon) changed
questions.hint: Compare Scene 1 Setting in (1) with Scene 2 Setting in (3)!
questions.explanation: A new scene begins when the time or place changes — here it moved from the castle morning to the garden treehouse at noon!

questions.instruction: Read the mini script and answer the question.

passage.title: Treehouse Club — Act 1, Scene 1
sentences: Characters: Sami, Nour, and Grandpa.
Setting: A wooden treehouse on Saturday afternoon.
Sami (holding a flashlight): Let's tell a funny story!
Nour (laughing): Okay, you go first!

questions.text: Which words in sentence (4) are Nour's DIALOGUE?
options: A wooden treehouse on Saturday afternoon.
questions.hint: Remember: dialogue is the words said out loud by a character (not the stage directions in parentheses)!
questions.explanation: 'Okay, you go first!' is Nour's dialogue (words spoken out loud), while '(laughing)' is stage directions!

questions.instruction: Read the mini script and answer the question.

passage.title: Treehouse Club — Act 1, Scene 1
sentences: Characters: Sami, Nour, and Grandpa.
Setting: A wooden treehouse on Saturday afternoon.
Sami (holding a flashlight): Let's tell a funny story!
Nour (laughing): Okay, you go first!

questions.text: What does sentence (1) show?
questions.hint: Sentence (1) lists everyone appearing in the play!
questions.explanation: Sentence (1) lists all of the characters in the play — the Cast of Characters!

questions.instruction: Read the mini script and decide if a new scene starts.

passage.title: Bake Sale Surprise
sentences: Setting: School gym at 9 o'clock in the morning.
Ben (putting cookies on a tray): Our table looks great!
Zara (waving to students): Here come our first customers!

questions.text: Next in the play, Maya walks up to the same table in the school gym at 9:05 in the morning. Should this stay in the SAME scene or start a NEW scene?
options: Stay in the same scene, because the place and time did not change
Start a new scene, because Maya walked in
Turn the play into a story book chapter
questions.answer: Stay in the same scene, because the place and time did not change
questions.hint: Ask: Did the setting (school gym, morning) change?
questions.explanation: A scene continues while the action stays in a single setting (same place and time)!

questions.instruction: Think about what happens at a scene change.
questions.text: The curtain closes for a moment while helpers move away the bedroom bed and roll out forest trees on stage. Why are they changing the stage?
options: Because the place is changing for a new scene
Because the actors forgot their dialogue
Because the playwright erased the script
questions.answer: Because the place is changing for a new scene
questions.hint: Bedroom → Forest means a new place!
questions.explanation: Changing the stage from a bedroom to a forest shows a new place, which means a new scene!

questions.instruction: Spot the missing Element of Drama.
questions.text: Read this line: 'Dragon ___: Watch out, here comes my sneeze!' Which part belongs in the blank to tell the actor what to do?
questions.hint: Which choice is a stage direction telling the actor what to do?
questions.explanation: (wiggling his nose) is a stage direction giving an action instruction to the actor!

questions.instruction: Spot ALL clues in a scene heading.
questions.text: Look at this heading in a script: 'ACT 1, SCENE 2 — Backyard Tent at Night.' Which part tells the SETTING?
questions.hint: Setting = the time AND place in the play!
questions.explanation: 'Backyard Tent' is the place and 'at Night' is the time — together they are the Setting!

questions.instruction: Check your Drama mastery!
questions.text: Which two changes can start a new scene in a play?
options: A change in time OR a change in place
A change in shirt OR a change in shoes
A loud clap OR a quiet whisper
A new narrator OR a longer script
questions.answer: A change in time OR a change in place
questions.hint: Remember our final slide: You will know it's a new scene when the ___ or ___ changes!
questions.explanation: You know it's a new scene whenever the time or place changes!
